conflicts: Feed dog: Janome's product page, brochure and Black Edition page say 5-piece, while its 2011 launch blog says 7-piece (our earlier spec took 7-piece from the blog); 5-piece is used.

Buttonhole: Janome's spec table and brochure say four-step while its page prose says one-step, and our earlier spec said one-step; no document explains a difference, so the spec table wording is used.
Stitch count: Janome's 2011 launch blog says 19, while its current page, brochure and manual say 18; 18 is used.
Zigzag width: the Key Features caption on the plain-machine page says 6 mm, while the spec table, brochure and manual say 6.5 mm; 6.5 mm is used.
Speed: 860 spm appears only in Janome's 2011 launch blog (and on the HD1000 page); the current HD3000 page, brochure and manual publish no speed, so max speed is left null.
Hook: our earlier spec said horizontal full rotary hook, while Janome says top loading full rotary hook; the maker wording is used.
Throat: Janome publishes only a workspace of 6.5 in wide by 4.6 in high, not a needle-to-arm figure, so throat is left null.

Warranty: Janome's generic warranty PDF gives 5 years for electronic parts, while our earlier note of 2 years electrical is not supported by that document (an Amazon listing may state 2 years; not checked).
Price: only Janome's MSRP is on record ($559 plain, $599 Black Edition), not a dealer price.

editorial.verdict: A mechanical aluminum-frame zigzag machine with 18 stitches and a rotary hook; owners split on heavy fabric and reliability, so check the dealer and return terms.
editorial.whoFor: Sewists who want a mechanical household machine with a dial foot-pressure control and an extra high foot lift for denim, canvas and mending.
editorial.skipIf: You need to sew thick leather or many layers every week, want a published top speed, or need a throat measured needle to arm.
editorial.keySpec: 18 stitches · 6.5 mm zigzag · 5-piece feed dog · 18.7 lb aluminum frame
strengths: Janome lists a top loading full rotary hook, a 5-piece feed dog and a foot-pressure dial, which its HD1000 page does not list.
Owners report it sewing thick work such as Cordura and duck canvas, though the 47 voices on heavy fabric split about evenly.
Janome states a 25 year limited warranty with 5 years on electronic parts and 1 year labor, void without an authorized US dealer purchase.
weaknesses: Owners report limits on heavy material: one could not sew denim, and another says the machine will not handle heavy leather.
Owners report jams, tension trouble and defects, with 19 of 38 reliability voices negative; Reddit over-represents problems.
Owners report a dim LED light that cannot be replaced, and the standard box has no walking or even feed foot.

checks.title: Which listing is it
checks.body: Amazon shows the plain HD3000 at 4.4 from 658 ratings and the Black Edition bundle at 4.4 from 333, as separate listings. The Sewing Machines Plus rating of 4.68 from 44 reviews has only 2 reviews naming this model, so it is not used as HD3000 evidence.

checks.title: Spec wording differs by Janome page
checks.body: Janome's own pages disagree on feed dog count, buttonhole step count, stitch count and zigzag width. Confirm 5-piece feed dog, 18 stitches and 6.5 mm on the listing, and do not read the HD1000 or HD5000 table as this model.

checks.title: Buy from an authorized US dealer
checks.body: Janome's generic warranty PDF says the warranty is void if the machine was not bought from an authorized Janome dealer in the United States. Verify the terms against the PDF and the dealer before buying from a marketplace seller.

realCost: Walking foot: not in the standard box; Janome lists an even feed foot as optional and as a Black Edition bonus item ($599 MSRP against $559 plain)
Heavy needles: Janome's chart puts heavy fabric at #14/90 to #16/100, and its leather guide uses 90/14 for seams and 100/16 for topstitching
Authorized dealer purchase: required for the warranty to stand, so a marketplace discount can cost the cover

faqs.q: Is the Janome HD3000 better than the Singer 4423?
faqs.a: Head-to-head owner claims in our rollup (4 in all) lean to the HD3000 on reliability, build and range of fabrics, which is a small sample. A PatternReview thread called the Singer the value buy and the HD3000 the smoother, quieter machine. Janome publishes no top speed for the HD3000.

faqs.q: Can the Janome HD3000 sew leather?
faqs.a: Janome's leather guide says to use leather thinner than 4 mm, under 2 mm when sewing through more than 4 layers, with a 3 mm stitch length, pressure dial at 3 and a 90/14 needle for seams. The manual says household use only. Owners report mixed results: one says feed dogs marked leather, and another says it will not handle heavy leather.

faqs.q: Is the Janome HD3000 good for beginners?
faqs.a: Janome calls it a heavy duty machine perfect for a beginner, which is its claim. It is a mechanical dial machine with a foot-pressure dial. Owners report tension trouble in 5 of 9 voices on that theme, so check the bobbin winding and tension on a new unit.

faqs.q: How many stitches does the Janome HD3000 have, 18 or 19?
faqs.a: 18. Janome's product page, brochure and manual all say 18, with the manual dial running patterns 1 to 18 plus the buttonhole. Only Janome's 2011 launch blog says 19.

faqs.q: What is the difference between the Janome HD3000 and HD1000?
faqs.a: From Janome's pages: the HD3000 lists 18 stitches, a 5-piece feed dog, a top loading full rotary hook, 6.5 mm width, 18.7 lb and $559 MSRP. The HD1000 lists 14 stitches, a 3-piece feed dog, a front-loading oscillating hook, 5 mm width, 16.8 lb and $409 MSRP. Owners also say the HD3000 pedal is more sensitive, which is Reddit only.

faqs.q: Does the Janome HD3000 have a walking foot?
faqs.a: Not in Janome's standard accessory list. An even feed foot is optional, and the Black Edition lists one as a bonus item. Owner reports differ: one says there is no true walking foot, and others say one came with their machine.

faqs.q: Is the Janome HD3000 good for quilting?
faqs.a: Janome lists a quilting guide bar and publishes a workspace of 6.5 in wide by 4.6 in high, not a needle-to-arm throat, so it is not a mid-arm machine. One former owner on Reddit reports making queen quilts on it and calling it very solid.

faqs.q: What is the Janome HD3000 Black Edition?
faqs.a: Janome's spec table matches the plain machine. The Black Edition lists $599 MSRP against $559 and adds bonus items such as an Ultra Glide foot, a leather needle set and an even feed foot. Dealer SKU HD3000BE is the Black Edition.

faqs.q: How fast is the Janome HD3000?
faqs.a: Janome's current page, brochure and manual publish no speed. The 860 spm figure appears only in Janome's 2011 launch blog and on the HD1000 page, so it is not stated here as an HD3000 spec.

faqs.q: Is the Janome HD3000 the same as the HD5000?
faqs.a: Janome's HD5000 spec table matches the HD3000 line for line, and the page names no difference. Treat any claimed difference as unverified.
